how: Repeated invitations recruit participants to start and sustain the room's logo.
The desire to cannibalize a rival logo is checked by having nobody available to help.
Successive members propose the mark without their role requiring others to join.
The initial proposer subsequently calls for as many helpers as possible.
The meeting-point invitation receives a report that the top row is nearly complete.
The shared-heart proposal receives a bare commitment to join.
A proposal receives assent that asks for nothing in return.
Conditional assent asks for an outline before joining and receives a later outline completion report.
A participant asks what the canvas is and then reports figuring it out and placing a red tile.
After placement ends, questions receive an explanation of pixel turf wars and the five-minute cooldown.
Post-close explanations support retrospective understanding rather than more placements on the completed canvas.
A working-side correction receives an apology and promised fix without demonstrating distress or a personal quarrel.
Participants choose a pixel logo and consider simpler text as an alternative.
The shared heart is revised into a white shape with a red-and-yellow checker.
A proposed slogan addition is tested against available space and neighboring marks.
Coordinates, four corners, and mockup adjustments make the shared mark locatable and reproducible.
Participants report the nearly complete top row and the visible top of the logo.
Builders identify mistaken blocks and working sides before redistributing revised design instructions.
A posted plan remains revisable during construction rather than necessarily settling design discussion once.
Discord invitations direct helpers into chat and answer a request for a chat venue.
Visible coordinate agreement cannot establish whether unseen chat coordination included decided leadership or assigned work.
The script reported by a visiting ally does not establish machine placement by the host room.
Explaining a cooldown and calling the event fun do not establish individual scheduling constraints or participation costs.
The ordinary cooldown explanation supplies no report of site malfunction or technical repair.
Chat invitations do not establish concealment, infiltration, or concern about rivals reading the plan.
Participants prepare defence against an alleged takeover and warn about a perimeter breach.
A report of construction is followed by calls to defend the emerging mark.
An overwriting accusation receives a denial of subreddit responsibility and a claim of helping clean the ally's mark.
A perceived threatening mark is identified as friendly neighboring artwork.
Wrong-block correction and changed instructions alone do not demonstrate uninformed keepers erasing an agreed design.
An outsider hypothesis cannot establish that failed notification caused repair of an obsolete form or loss of a planned change.
Defence and a neighboring script are visible while own-room automation adoption remains unseen.
Participants search for open space, choose coordinates, and adjust the mockup during construction.
Expected domination by a competing group prompts an upward move before a verified erasure of that attempt.
Anticipatory relocation should not be treated as rebuilding after a verified loss merely because another turn reports a later loss.
Insufficient hands can produce withdrawal or diversion to another project rather than relocation.

statement: restarting after a participant declares withdrawal
how: A later participant resumes work after another declares abandonment without evidence that the announcement bound everyone or caused the restart.
A neighbor proposes coexistence and the room announces a treaty requiring restraint.
Participants explicitly order others to spare neighboring work.
Border negotiation can occur during construction while outlining continues.
The treaty announcement expressly names the agreement as grounds for not damaging the neighboring logo.
Help includes spare turns, requests for visibility, a further project invitation, and reciprocal defence promises.
Completion of another project can release help without a stated shortage driving the exchange.
A participant explicitly attributes equal defence of the ally's logo to discovering the alliance.
A treaty is honored through a proposed shared heart that participants agree to build and revise.
An imagined alliance and local assent do not establish that the named other groups joined.
Treaty commemoration can explicitly motivate joint work when a common-threat mechanism is unshown.
A member reports carrying a request for use of a spot to another group.
The request for permission to use a spot fits the entry's minimum range of asking a host for space.
A space request and surviving treaty title do not establish host approval or subsequent governance.
A member states a personal limit on honoring the treaty because of another sports allegiance.
A post naming an existing treaty receives an explicit refusal to honor it, fitting refusal after agreement.
Dual supporters identify and recognize their shared affiliations across the neighboring teams.
A participant explicitly claims both team identities while calling for coexistence.
Shared subreddit membership does not imply shared loyalties toward an alliance partner.
A treaty reminder after placement closes evidences restraint in discussion without demonstrating prevention of new pixel changes.
Treaty instructions and an overwriting complaint do not establish an argument about whether covering artwork is morally fair.
Inherited sports rivalry supplies the named target of a proposed hostile inscription.
A familiar anti-rival refrain is carried into a proposed canvas inscription.
A familiar rival is named in the same turn that proposes cannibalizing its logo.
Participants joke about transformed logos and the rival's altered spelling.
An existing sports room's chat invitation does not establish formation of a new canvas faction.
Demands to stop fake injury posts concern separate April Fools conduct rather than policing offensive canvas talk.
Fake injury reports receive both appreciation for the prank and demands for bans.
False Celtics allegiance is identified as April Fools material and challenged as poor content.
Participants explicitly identify April Fools copypasta and remake it around a different player.
Reusable parody is rewritten while other replies return to serious basketball argument.
Visible complaints concern Celtics prank threads and injury jokes rather than explicit containment of canvas posts.
Calls and a moderator's progress report do not establish a flood of canvas posts causing a containment rule.
Proposed attacks on other marks do not demonstrate a self-attack motivated by resentment of canvas posts.
Members celebrate completion and thank the contributors.
The fixed final logo receives an immediate collective success celebration.
Participants recount successive logos and use a timelapse to locate the remembered takeover.
Recording can elicit celebration within an episode instead of always following it.
After placement ends, a fixed copy is presented and a commenter thanks its maker for removing an annoying pixel.
Correcting a preferred copy does not by itself establish a wider dispute over which historical version should survive.
Replacement described as occurring in a picture after placement closes is image editing rather than a new canvas attack.
An ally greets the finished work and receives a reciprocal welcome, fitting the entry's ally-visitor route.
An ally greeting does not establish subscriber growth or discovery of the room through the canvas mark.
Contributor thanks and internal celebration do not establish seeking the team's or press's attention.
Preservation celebrations and alliance thanks do not establish a successor canvas or enduring joint institution.
The record supplies preservation and alliance credit without an evidenced transition to a continuing project.
Participants propose recoloring an encroaching image and hijacking or cannibalizing existing marks.
The logo invitation receives a proposal to turn an encroaching duck red.
Lack of helpers answers an attack proposal as a capacity obstacle rather than restraint toward the target.
A proposal to take neighboring space receives a reminder of the existing treaty.
An answer after placement closes supports discursive restraint without showing that it stopped an executable attack.
Members retrospectively laugh about logo transformations and the rival's altered spelling.
The particular attack proposal that produced the narrated takeover cannot be identified from the surviving recollections.
